Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 30-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE, MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Human Computer Interaction [NPT_4131]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Construct a mid-fidelity prototype for a healthcare mobile application. Build a user flow that        (5)  
  demonstrates navigation between key screens, and model how user feedback at this stage could  
  A)           refine the final high-fidelity prototype.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Categorize the main interaction types in HCI (Instructing, Conversing, Manipulating, Exploring, and   (3)  
  Responding). Distinguish their unique roles, and explain the function of multimodal interaction in  
  enhancing user experience.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Analyze the relationship between SECI and IoT to determine how user-centered design principles        (2)  
  enable effective communication between humans and connected devices.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Build a short step-by-step plan outlining how you would gather qualitative data through semi-         (5)  
  structured interviews for a usability study of an online learning platform.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Apply the concept of IRB approval to a research scenario involving user testing of a mental health    (3)  
  app. Explain how ethical standards and participant consent should be maintained.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Apply the concept of IRB approval to explain why a researcher studying gamified interfaces must       (2)  
  include a plan for anonymizing participant data in their proposal.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Construct a prototyping plan for a new e-learning mobile app by outlining the sequence of steps you (5)  
  would take from lo-fi sketches to hi-fi prototypes. Explain how you would incorporateuser testing  
  A)           and stakeholder feedback at each stage.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Classify the tools mentioned (paper-pencil, Miro, Canva, Figma, Adobe XD) by the fidelity stage       (3)  
  where they are primarily used. Categorize each tool by its primary function. Justify each placement  
  
  Page #1

briefly  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Determine the most suitable fidelity level to demonstrate the design of a food delivery application     (2)  
  and justify your selection briefly.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Examine how user feedback influences transitions between different fidelity stages in the design        (5)  
  process. Draw an inference about how continuous user testing enhances usability and stakeholder  
  A)         confidence.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Determine an appropriate data analysis tool (R, SPSS, or NVivo) for a study focusing on emotional       (3)  
  responses in interface design, and justify your choice in one or two sentences.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Examine how continuous user feedback gathered through tools like Figma or Canva helps refine            (2)  
  design elements during the transition from Mid-Fi to Hi-Fi prototypes, and provide a brief inference  
  on the indicators that show a design is ready for stakeholder presentation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Construct a user-centered prototyping plan for a mobile healthcare application. Include the choice      (5)  
  of fidelity level (Lo-Fi, Mid-Fi, Hi-Fi), the prototyping tools, and the user feedback methods you  
  A)         would employ at each stage.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Compare the ethical requirements for IRB-approved research with the privacy and security                (3)  
  principles in SECI-based systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Identify two major ethical safeguards required during data gathering under the IRB approval             (2)  
  process and explain why they are essential in human-centered research.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
